Incorporating Beige Book insights (April to mid-May), the FOMC’s positive tone is broadly confirmed: districts reported ongoing economic expansion with tight labor markets across retail, business services, technical, manufacturing, and construction jobs. Contacts cited persistent hiring difficulties and rising wage pressures (modest to moderate), which, together with increasing benefit costs, reflect capacity constraints rather than demand weakness. Consumer spending and loan demand were generally steady to modestly higher across districts, but pricing in bank lending firmed and conditions in commercial real estate were mixed, indicating credit is not uniformly easier. Overall, this Beige Book evidence supports the Fed’s move to hike 25 bp and maintain guidance for gradual increases, while slightly tempering the outlook given labor constraints and firming cost/credit conditions.
